question.problem:
Find the value of the constant $a$ that makes the function $g(x)$ below continuous at $x=2.$

$$
g(x)=\{\begin{aligned}{3}^{2ax+1}, & x\le 2 \\ 2x+5, & x>2\end{aligned}
$$

current_example.problem:
Find the value of the constant $c$ that makes the function $h(x)$ below continuous at $x=4.$
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14193886/assets/5b758f403156100f70cb6d6fc5a8785dad6e8e073a39bba4f9ed1d08e627929c.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
At $x=4,$ the left-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {4}^{-}}h(x) & =h(4) \\  & ={4}^{c(4)+1} \\  & ={4}^{4c+1},\end{aligned}
$$

 

and the right-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {4}^{+}}h(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {4}^{+}}(4x) \\  & =4(4) \\  & =16.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for $h(x)$ to be continuous at $x=4,$ we require that

$$
\begin{aligned}{4}^{4c+1} & =16 \\ {4}^{4c+1} & ={4}^{2} \\ 4c+1 & =2 \\ 4c & =1 \\ c & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $h(x)$ is continuous at $x=4$ for $c = \dfrac{1}{4}.$
